The Commonwealth of Massachusetts
Executive Office of Environmental Affairs Department of Environmental Quality Engineering 190 Cambridge Street, Boston 02202
MEMORANDUM
SUBJECT: Kendall Square Urban Renewal
Project: Air Quality Analysis
TO: Ashvin Patel
MEPA Unit, EOEA
FROM: David Friend, DAHM
Stephen Dennis, DAHM Spo
DATE: August 9, 1977
The Division of Air and Hazardous Materials has received and reviewed copies of both the draft EIS for the Kendall Square Urban Renewal Project and the supporting Air Quality Analysis Report prepared by Metcalf & Eddy, Inc.
In our review of these documents, we are quite pleased to see the emphasis placed upon public transportation, smooth street traffic flow, adequate on-site bicycle storage facilities, and improved pedestrian access to the proposed site. Similarly, we strongly endorse the recommendation that on-street parking be prohibited at all times in the project area. In light of the projection that vehicular traffic will increase under all of the "Build" options, we cannot underscore enough the importance of smooth traffic flow conditions and adequate alternatives to the polluting motor vehicle.
There are several areas of concern, however, relative to the DEIS discussion and analysis of motor vehicle emissions. These concerns are outlined briefly below:
(1) Relationship of proposed project to the Boston TCP
Although the DEIS does summarize the elements of the Boston TCP, and does assign significant importance to motor vehicle emissions inspection and maintenance (I&M), several other relevant TCP strategies must not be slighted. For example, the parking freeze regulation (40 CFR s. 52.1135) establishes a "freeze" as of October 15, 1973 on the construction of new commercial parking facilities in the City of Cambridge. Subsequently, if the proposed development does contain a number of parking spaces defined as "commercial" under the scope of the freeze regulation, it will be necessary for the developer to secure a Commercial Parking Permit from this Department. This state approval will be necessary until the authority to issue Commercial Parking Permits has been delegated to the City of CAmbridge (Note: it is expected that this delegation of authority will occur in the near future).
